recentItems.title: NATO in the ARCTIC & NORTHERN DEFENSE: Iceland’s defense chief reveals some details
recentItems.description:
Iceland’s Chief of Defence, Jónas G. Allansson, reaffirmed the country’s commitment to collective defence on NATO’s northern flank. He noted that the Alliance’s 32-member defence system works in coordination through regular joint exercises and patrols.

Although Iceland has no standing army of its own, it remains a strategically important security hub in the North Atlantic. Iceland hosts allied operations and contributes to NATO’s surveillance and situational awareness in the Greenland–Iceland–United Kingdom (GIUK) Gap, a key corridor between Europe and North America.

recentItems.title: YANDEX BLACKOUT, MOSCOW AIRPORTS paralyzed, and an oil refinery in flames 1,400 KM AWAY!
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Volodarskaya oil pumping station near Moscow, which supplies aviation fuel to three Russian capital-region airports. Ukraine says that 51% of Russia’s oil-refining capacity has been disabled. The Salavat refinery, around 1,400 km from Ukraine, was also attacked, along with a “shadow fleet” tanker near Sochi, the Sasta machine-tool plant in Ryazan region, and a Yandex data centre.

Against the backdrop of these attacks, September was a record month for Ukraine’s Armed Forces in destroying Russian air-defence assets; Ukrainian military figures also report 33,087 Russian troops killed. The effectiveness of Ukrainian weapons prompted the Pentagon to place a second order for F10 drones, while NATO’s Military Committee visited Kyiv for the first time in eight years to study Ukraine’s combat experience.

recentItems.title: MISSILE STRIKE ON KYIV, as “SAMARA” FACILITY IN RUSSIA attacked FOR THE SECOND TIME THIS MONTH
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump’s statements about a deal with Vladimir Putin to supply Russian diesel to the global market drew sharp criticism from Ukraine. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the decision “weak” and warned that allowing Russia to export petroleum products is a direct investment in Russia’s war machine — and that Moscow will repay it with more terror.

The night of October 10 confirmed those warnings: Russian forces attacked Kyiv with jet-powered Shahed drones and ballistic missiles, striking energy infrastructure facilities.
